text:
support_jen: @kevin @maria escalating ACME (private VPC / on-prem) — customer reports sudden 429 bursts and auth failures after a traffic spike. p99 latency jumped to ~3.8s and error rate to 8%. They say it started after they changed their frontend to do aggressive retry-with-jitter. :warning:

acme_ops: seeing 429s from our side too. Clients report 401 on the first few requests sometimes, then 429 on bursts. We attached last 10k request log sample.

ingress-bot: env: acme-prod, svc: customer-gateway, ingress: nginx-ingress-controller-1 (k8s 1.24)

kevin: thanks. can you paste the ingress annotations + envoy/ratelimit config (if any)? also need a repro curl that triggers the behavior.

acme_ops: ingress annotations are minimal. here's what we added recently:

```
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "200"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/enable-rate-limit: "true"
```

and our gateway pods run an Envoy sidecar that talks to a redis-backed rate-limit-service. env vars: RATE_LIMIT_SERVICE=redislabs://rls.local:6379, BUCKET_MODE=token_bucket.

maria: a couple immediate flags:
- those nginx annotations limit per-ingress controller instance, not globally. with multiple replicas the effective global limit is replicas*limit unless you have global RL service coordinated.
- burst 200 is high relative to bucket refill. token_bucket burst should be tuned to absorb short spikes, not sustain them.
- 401s on first request hints at auth handshake latency / token fetch race — retries may be causing double load.

phil: also check kube-proxy / node-level conntrack / kubelet limits. If the frontend is opening many short-lived connections, you can saturate ephemeral ports / NAT and see 5xx/401/odd errors in the gateway.

kevin: agree. what I'd like to collect right now:
1) kubectl get pods -l app=customer-gateway -n acme -o wide
2) kubectl logs -l app=customer-gateway -n acme --tail=400 | grep -E "429|401|error"
3) curl repro: we'll provide a synthetic burst test (below)
4) /metrics from envoy and rate-limit service (counters: rate_limit_allowed, rate_limit_denied, bucket_fill_rate)

maria: repro curl to mimic their frontend retries:

```
for i in {1..300}; do
  (curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://acme-gateway.internal/api/generate &)
  sleep 0.01
done
wait
```

kevin: running that locally against a replica reproduced 429s. I captured envoy /ratelimit responses showing token_bucket_allow=true for some requests and deny for others. sample Envoy header block:

```
x-envoy-rate-limit: true
x-envoy-rate-limit-headers: x-client-id
x-rate-limit-reason: token_bucket_exhausted
```

phil: remediation suggestions prioritized: short-term (minutes) -> medium-term (hours) -> long-term (days):
- short-term: temporarily scale gateway replicas to absorb burst and reduce ingress controller pod counts so nginx annotations act more predictably; OR reduce frontend retry aggressiveness. Also set nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps to lower value per-pod to reduce burst amplification.
- medium-term: enable global rate-limit service coordination (central token store e.g., redis) and tune token refill rates and max-burst to realistic values (burst <= ~2x steady rps for your workload).
- long-term: revise frontend client logic to use exponential backoff + jitter, add a circuit-breaker in gateway to return Retry-After headers, and instrument per-client quotas in our rate-limit service.

maria: concrete config snippet for Envoy token-bucket (example):

```
route:
  rate_limits:
  - stage: 0
    actions:
    - request_headers:
        header_name: "x-client-id"
        descriptor_key: "client"
    - generic_key:
        descriptor_value: "global"
    token_bucket:
      max_tokens: 200
      tokens_per_fill: 10
      fill_interval: 1s
```

Note: tokens_per_fill and fill_interval define refill. With max_tokens 200 and 10/s refill, a sustained 500 RPS will exhaust bucket quickly. For ACME their steady RPS is ~80 so set values close to that, e.g., max_tokens: 120, tokens_per_fill: 80 per 1s, burst 40.

kevin: for immediate triage I did: scaled replicas from 2 -> 6, temporarily set nginx limit-rps to 60 and limit-burst to 80, and disabled frontend aggressive retries (they rolled back). p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 420ms and 429s fell to ~0.8%.

acme_ops: confirmed improvement. but want to avoid recurring config changes. what do we need from us?

support_jen: next steps / action items:
- ACME: keep frontend rollback for 24h and monitor.
- SRE (kevin/maria): schedule runbook update for private VPC troubleshooting and recommended default rate-limiter profiles for on-prem customers. include: recommended nginx/ingress + envoy token-bucket defaults, diag commands, and metric names.
- Product (phil): consider exposing a "burst smoothing" toggle in the Console for Dedicated/Private that atomically adjusts ingress & envoy settings.
- Support: schedule 30m call with ACME ops tomorrow to walk through root cause and timeline.

maria: I'll draft the recommended rate-limit profiles. quick list to include in runbook:
- expected steady RPS for service and recommended tokens_per_fill (aligned to capacity)
- burst ceiling <= 2x steady RPS
- per-client quotas + Retry-After header logic
- ingress controller: prefer global RL or use an external rate-limit service rather than per-pod nginx annotations for consistent behavior
- probes to watch: envoy_rate_limit_allowed_total, envoy_rate_limit_denied_total, envoy_request_duration_seconds{quantile="0.99"}, kube_node_conntrack_entries

phil: also note billing exposure: retries multiplied token consumption. ask billing team to mark spike as "investigation" to avoid auto-invoice escalations if we can show mitigation and config changes.

support_jen: thanks everyone. I'll capture the logs/metrics link and the customer call invite. tagging follow-ups: @kevin (runbook PR), @maria (profile YAMLs), @phil (console product request). :thumbsup:

acme_ops: we appreciate the quick help. we'll keep the frontend change blocked until the call.

ingress-bot: incident-note: temporary scale & nginx throttle applied by kevin at 2028-06-14T15:40:12Z

support_jen: closing thread for now — will reopen if we see re-regression after the 24h window.
